data.hypothesis: The previous arithmetic variant failed one row at N=16384 after combining reciprocal-square-root approximation with cancellation of target mass. This experiment isolates the reciprocal-square-root change: retain T1's tiled kernel, target-mass multiplication, and final mass division, while replacing the square-root denominator with rsqrtf(distSq) cubed. This may retain a math-throughput benefit with less numerical deviation, but must be checked and measured.

memory_lessons.applicability: When an arithmetic rewrite fails, isolate its transformations rather than assuming which one caused the error; validate the revised formula on all cases before timing.
memory_lessons.claim: The direct-acceleration variant passed all but one checked output row at N=16384 and produced no timings. It combined target-mass cancellation with rsqrtf cubing, so the failure does not identify either transformation as the cause.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Retain the target-mass factor and final division while testing rsqrtf cubing on the T1 base.

data.notes: Only src/nbody_kernel.cu changes; the T1 launch configuration remains block=128, items_per_block=128, shared_memory_bytes=4096. This restores target-mass multiplication and final division while retaining rsqrtf cubing. The revised candidate has not been checked or measured; no performance or correctness claim is made.
transformations: Retain T1's shared-memory source tiling and one-target-per-thread mapping.
Replace sqrtf(distSq) and the denominator division with rsqrtf(distSq) cubed using multiplications.
Restore target-mass multiplication in the interaction and final division by target mass to avoid combining two unvalidated arithmetic changes.
